serverTtfb.method: plain Node fetch to first response byte, no browser, no CPU or network emulation
serverTtfb.note: The browser TTFB above includes the emulated RTT (150ms on the mobile profile) and the browser's own scheduling. This figure is the server render on its own.

perceivedResponsiveness.method: in-page click on an in-app nav link, timed to the first DOM mutation on the same clock

authorization.discriminator: main#dashboard-content presence (primary); nav-link count is corroborating evidence and the fallback for captures predating this field
authorization.verdict: every measured sample rendered an authorized shell

hydration.verdict: no React hydration mismatch was logged on any measured navigation

contentAssertion.verdict: every measured sample rendered real page content

settle.verdict: every sample was taken after the DOM went quiet, so late-arriving data is inside the measurement

hostContention.method: os.cpus() idle/total tick deltas over a 1000ms window; the baseline is taken before the browser launches, the second reading after it exits

busyPercentDuringRun.note: includes this capture's own browser and driver, so its ceiling is higher than the pre-launch one; judged on the median so a single transient burst does not refuse a good run

hostContention.verdict: the host was quiet enough for these timings to be the application's

conditions.mobile: 390x844@3x, 4x CPU, 1.6 Mbps down / 750 Kbps up, 150ms RTT
conditions.authMethod: minted NextAuth session cookie, set once via CDP and reused for every navigation
conditions.themeNote: The app reads its theme from localStorage["streamlineos-app-theme-mode"] and falls back to DEFAULT_APP_THEME_MODE ("light"), consulting prefers-color-scheme only when the stored value is "system". This run wrote "light" into that key before every document, so the emulated media feature and the rendered theme agree; emulating prefers-color-scheme alone would have measured light while claiming dark.
conditions.cache: vitals navigations run with the HTTP cache enabled after one discarded warm-up; firstLoadBytesByRoute is a separate cache-disabled pass
conditions.serverModeDerivation: the build id in the served HTML is compared against .next/BUILD_ID; it is not asserted by this driver

host.loadAverageNote: os.loadavg() is NOT implemented on this platform and returns 0 — recorded as null rather than as an idle host. Read hostContention instead.
host.note: A throttled mobile profile on a contended host measures the host. hostContention carries the measured figure this run was judged on.
